sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Configure maximum Pods per node (GKE)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: with the default of 110 Pods 'Kubernetes assigns a /24 CIDR block (256 addresses) to each of the nodes'; the block holds at least twice the maximum Pods; the worked example: 110 Pods per node and a /21 Pod range give 2^(24-21) = 8 nodes; maximum Pods per node 'cannot' be changed after the cluster or node pool is created, but a new node pool can set its own; when Pod addresses run out, 'you can create additional Pod IP address ranges using discontiguous multi-Pod CIDR'. The gcloud flags (--add-secondary-ranges, --pod-ipv4-range) are from memory of the CLI reference (to verify).

sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Troubleshoot VPC-native clusters (GKE)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: the error '[IP_SPACE_EXHAUSTED] Instance ... creation failed: IP space of ... is exhausted'; each node reserves a contiguous block from the cluster's Pod range even if few Pods run; if the name in the error is [SUBNET_NAME]-[SECONDARY_RANGE_NAME]-[HASH] the Pod range is exhausted, if it is only the subnet name the node range is; remedies: add Pod IPv4 ranges (discontiguous multi-Pod CIDR) without re-creating the cluster, expand the subnet's primary range with expand-ip-range when nodes run out, or create a node pool with a smaller maximum Pods per node (110 reserves a /24, 32 a /26).
